recipes.name: Creamy Green Beans Parmesan
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh green beans, trimmed and snapped

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly-salted water to a boil; drop in the green beans and return to a boil. Cook uncovered until the beans are bright green and barely tender, about 6 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat; whisk the cream, 2 tablespoons of Parmesan cheese, and nutmeg into the melted butter. Bring the mixture to a simmer. Gently stir the beans into the mixture to coat; season with salt and pepper. Return to a simmer, transfer to a serving dish, and sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of Parmesan cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Green Beans Parmesan
raw_recipe.description: Fresh green beans get a simple but delicious sauce made with cream, Parmesan cheese, and a hint of nutmeg.

review.reviewBody: I love this sauce! I make this same sauce for my pork chops!!! The only thing I do different is instead of using nutmeg, I use garlic powder :)

These were excellent and I loved the sauce. The only reason I gave a 4 instead of a 5 was that I had to double the sauce(like many suggested in the comments) or else there would have not been enough for a full lb of fresh green beans. I did steam them instead of boiling and as far as the parm, I used reg. grated parm in the sauce and then fresh grated parm on top at the end.

I have made this recipe several times. It's our family go to for green beans as side dish. I do double or triple the sauce and I added cream cheese 1 oz per serving ie; the recipe states it serves 4 so I put 1oz of cream cheese. If I change to 8 servings then it would be 2 oz of cream cheese.

So good! I used a 12 oz package of frozen green beans that I cooked in the microwave. I did the sauce on the stove and then added the beans to that. I used half & half instead of the heavy cream. This was so creamy and tasty. Thanks!
I steamed a 1 lb package of fresh green beans. Doubled the sauce and made as directed. Before serving, sprinkled garlic salt on top and everyone kept going back for seconds.
This recipe is great! But double the sauce! Do not leave out the nutmeg it's what makes it so great. I also added cooked diced bacon, made this recipe most requested side in my house!!!

This was wonderful and my family loved it! Knowing that my family prefer a generousamout of any sauces and toppings, etc., I doubled the sauce portion of the rcipe. If your family is the same way, it is easy enough to do. Double the butter, cream, and first of the Parmesan cheese. If your family prefers just a subtle hint of topping, then follow the recipe as written. I prefer to steam green beans, so that's what I did. Basically just cook the beans how you like them, then make your sauce and add the beans. So very easy and delicous, too. We like cheese, but only used one tablespoon to sprinkle on before serving. If you have an ounce of common sense, you can make this to suit your taste buds. This was a wonderful addition to my dinner presentation. Thank you for this fine recipe. By the way, I was fairly generous with the nutmeg, but didn't even notice it. I guess it did blend in afterall.

The amounts required are wrong! I made the sauce as written and it was too dry. It barely coated the green beans. The sauce tasted great, but I would not make it as written again. You should double the sauce recipe.
It was good, but parmesan sticked to the non stick pan. I also added some garlic and it was tastier than the first time.

I printed out this recipe at work so I could make these to go with dinner last night. I drove home only to realize I left the recipe on my desk. Had to try to remember the ingredients and it looks like all I forgot was the milk or cream. I steamed my haricot verts in the micro for 4 minutes, while I melted some butter in the pan. Tossed in some nutmeg and parmesan, enough to coat but certainly not enough to become a sauce. Stirred the beans into that buttery goodness, sprinkled with coarse ground black pepper and kosher salt and they were delicious!!! I was only sorry that my husband loved them as much as I did, because there were none left when I went back for seconds. LOL. So, if you want a lighter version, do what I did by mistake. Great recipe!

OH MY GOD! These were the second best green beans I've ever had in my life! (My favorite recipe is sweet green bean bundles from this site but those are covered in sugar and wrapped in bacon so that's sorta cheating) I used a little less than a full pound of green beans so they were a bit saucier than they would have been making them exactly as stated. My husband and I both hate fresh green beans so I've been searching for a recipe that would make them appetizing for us. This is it! I did steam them rather than boiling and cooked them past "barely tender" to suit our tastes. I used 1/8 tsp of nutmeg and found it was the perfect amount. I also used Sargento's Artisan blend Parmesan but I don't know if that makes much difference. I recommend trying this even if you aren't crazy about nutmeg or fresh green beans. I will be making these for company and look forward to trying it on asparagus. Thank you for a great recipe!

I've never been a fan of fresh green beans and had good intentions. But, due to our current drought conditions, we were unable to get fresh locally. I ended up using canned, minus the salt and nutmeg, added some chopped garlic and fresh basil, and substituted half and half for the heavy cream. Using recipe quantities, I had just enough sauce for a 14.5 ounce can for 2 people. It tasted pretty darned good, in spite of my changes. Even my fussy husband asked for more (which I didn't have). This would probably work well with frozen green beans, too. It's a keeper in my book.

YES! I've had this recipe saved and I've been making these for years. If you want to make green beans more exciting, fancy, or even kid-friendly, this is the perfect recipe. I love making it as a side dish for Italian food. I don't change anything with this recipe!
Easy and yummy!
It is so good, I wanted it a bit more saucy, so I upped the proportions of cream, butter & cheese with no regrets.

I'm currently 6 months pregnant and that might make me a little fonder of food than usual, buuuut... this was absolutely delicious. I may or may not have eaten the entire thing. And I may or may not have licked my plate clean. (I totally did)
Enjoyed the flavor, but needed more salt
Nice side dish. Need to work on texture of the sauce.
Excellent recipe. My family cannot get enough of it . My son even loved it. I wish I would have found thid recipe years ago.
This is a nice change from the usual plain green beans. Added some nice richness and flavor. Thanks!
